title: Study problem: a defective record after Vermont Yankee
shortTitle: Study problem: a defective record after Vermont Yankee
summary: A challenger must distinguish an actual defect in a rule’s evidentiary justification from a preference for additional procedures that might reveal a defect.
notes:
Assume participants wanted cross-examination of a technical study and the agency refused. One proposed argument is that a better hearing might have produced a better record. Another identifies a concrete unresolved flaw in the study that leaves the final rule inadequately supported. The notes ask how these arguments differ after Vermont Yankee.

The decision bars courts from routinely adding preferred procedural devices to § 553, but leaves review of the rule’s justification intact. The substantive argument therefore requires identifying a real deficiency, while an abstract demand for extra procedures may only hypothesize one. Nova Scotia and American Radio Relay raise the adjacent question whether disclosing the critical study is already part of statutory meaningful comment. Kavanaugh and Levin offer opposing accounts of that interpretive boundary. The exercise has no reported case disposition; it organizes the competing arguments and their burdens.
